name: Public records access and information requests
one_line: The answering authority's own file for one request for recorded information: the received request, the search record, the item-by-item disclosure schedule, the redacted release, the withheld original, the refusal or partial refusal, and any internal review or oversight-body appeal. It is not activated by an access statute, an exemption citation, a reference-shaped token, or the presence of redaction; it requires the holder to be the body answering an external request, and it is the one government situation whose organizing anchor is a stranger's request rather than the authority's own programme.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are schema-activation signals for the government schema, which declares no fields. No accepted signal licenses writing a request, requester, exemption, or release fact. Every signal must evidence the holder as the body ANSWERING an external request, not as a requester, recipient, or reader of a disclosure.

one request reference repeated across an inbound request, an acknowledgement, a search record, a schedule, a decision letter, and a review, where the deciding or sending block is the holding public body; the same reference printed on a requester's copy is excluded by the role precondition

a document-level disclosure schedule: repeated item rows carrying a document description, a document date, a per-item disposition such as release, part-release, or withhold, and a per-item exemption or redaction reason - the signature structure of this row and of no other government row

a decision or refusal letter carrying all of a date the request was received, a response-due or statutory-response date, a disposition, and a rights-of-review or complaint paragraph addressed to the requester

a disclosure or publication log register: one row per request, with a request reference, a date received, a summary of what was asked, an outcome column, and a requester field that is anonymised or absent by design
a search or retrieval record naming systems, mailboxes, custodians, search terms, dates searched, and nil returns, tied to an exact request reference
a redacted release and an unredacted original of the SAME item set sitting under one request reference - a version family whose members have deliberately opposite exposure
an oversight-body case reference from an information commissioner, ombudsman, or tribunal paired with the authority's own request reference, plus the authority's submissions or chronology
a fee, cost-estimate, extension, transfer-to-another-authority, or repeat-and-burdensome determination notice that cites the same request reference and is issued by the holder
a case-management export or archive manifest whose paths repeatedly encode one request reference across request, correspondence, search, schedule, and bundle families
needs_llm: deciding WHICH SIDE holds a disclosure bundle when the released copy is byte-identical for the authority, the requester, a journalist, a campaigner, a lawyer, and a researcher; interpretation may use only a bounded local dossier and must abstain when custody is unresolved
recognizing an unlabeled public-interest-test note, harm assessment, or exemption rationale whose function is expressed only in prose with no headed slots

separating an access-regime request from a subject-access or personal-data request in which the requester asks about themselves; the latter is a named person's own record and routes away from this row
deciding whether a redacted bundle is an authority's disclosure workflow or a legal, research, or reading packet after identifiers have been minimized
distinguishing an authority's disclosure schedule from a litigation or discovery schedule that itemises documents and withholding reasons in the same columnar shape
deciding whether a hybrid, arms-length, contracted-out, or quasi-public body is answering as a public authority at all; abstain rather than guess
judging whether an item inside a released bundle is a member of this request or merely a similar record held elsewhere in the corpus
abstaining whenever no external request workflow can be cited, however much access vocabulary is present
never_alone: an access-regime statute name, an exemption or clause citation, or phrases such as public interest test, vexatious, or neither confirm nor deny; the requester's copy, an archives access review, a lawyer's advice note, and a campaigner's template letter all carry the same vocabulary
a request-shaped reference token such as FOI-2026-0412 or 2026-0412; the identical string is printed on the requester's copy, quoted in a news article, and pasted into a campaigning site

redaction itself - black boxes, a REDACTED stamp, exemption codes in the page footer, or a redaction watermark; redaction is a treatment applied in litigation productions, published court exhibits, journalism, and research anonymisation, and never proves a disclosure workflow
a disclosure log, transparency page, or open-data release downloaded for reference; publication by an authority is not authority-side custody
a public body's name, seal, letterhead, .gov-style domain, or officer signature block; the body may be the requester's target, a cited authority, or the sender of a document held by its recipient
a folder or filename containing FOI, Freedom of Information, Disclosure, Transparency, Access to Information, EIR, or Records Request

a member of the public's name and address appearing beside an authority's name; a person plus an organisation is never-alone evidence twice over and may equally describe casework, a complaint, or a mailing list
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a shared download session or a single browser batch that pulled several disclosure PDFs together; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
the absence of camera metadata on an image, used as proof that it is a case-queue or request-portal screenshot
a statutory-looking deadline or a countdown of working days; deadline cadence occurs in casework, procurement, planning, complaints, and litigation alike

work_types: schedule of documents or disclosure schedule
fee notice, cost estimate, or extension notice
response, decision, part-refusal, or refusal letter
internal review request and review decision
disclosure log or publication-scheme register entry
grouping_reasons: one request lifecycle, linked by an exact request reference across receipt, clarification, search, schedule, decision, release, review, and appeal; the appeal additionally carries the oversight body's own case reference and both references anchor the same group

records disclosed inside a bundle are MEMBERS of the request group and keep their own schema evidence; a released procurement evaluation, inspection report, mailbox extract, or personal record does not acquire request, exemption, or release facts from membership, and its own row does not acquire the request either

the redacted release and the unredacted source set form a version family with deliberately opposite exposure; version-family reasoning must not propagate released status, low sensitivity, or publication from the redacted copy to the original
a disclosure log is a register of requests, not a group of the underlying records; a log row does not pull the referenced records into any group
a case export or archive manifest stays shallow until its internal access boundaries are known and is never unpacked merely to strengthen recognition
sparse members such as a bare chase email or an unnamed schedule join only through an exact reference and are marked as grouped without copying facts
no group is a valid outcome; an isolated notice or bundle routes to a residual rather than being forced into a request lifecycle

template.why: Empty by contract: PR-6 leaves the government schema with no fields and D1's deferral stands, so a template on it cannot branch on any declared field. The world nevertheless has a clear prose order that R1c may adjudicate later: the bounded request comes first, then the stage of the response cycle, then the individual item; the requester must never become an organizing dimension, because a branch named after a member of the public discloses both that the person asked and what they asked about. Time is not first because “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders” - a request opened in December and answered in February would otherwise be split. Any later order remains editable: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE: FOIA response - City Water Dept.pdf and the request bundle archive. The bytes are identical on both sides. THIS ROW requires the answering authority's own process around the release - receipt, search record, schedule, exemption reasoning, decision issued outward, review rights. The journalism row requires the requester's side, resolved by a story slug, a draft, or fact-check apparatus. RECIPROCAL: this row must not claim a reporter's obtained bundle merely because it carries a statute and a reference number, and the journalism row must not claim an authority's own disclosure file. Where neither structure is present the covering letter is a standalone document with a durable purpose and no group.

SAME FIXTURE: a document that names a reference and refuses or defers access with exemption-shaped reasoning. Both sit on the records-holder side. THIS ROW requires an external request workflow - a requester, a request reference, a response clock, and an answer sent outward; Access Review for MS-0603-14 closed until 2059 is the archives row's, keyed to an accessioned item and an opening date. Disclosure Schedule for FOI Request 2026-118 is this row's. RECIPROCAL and consistent with the landed archives node: a redaction record alone decides nothing on either side.

SAME FIXTURE: RE Case 8841 - third chase.eml. Both hold a request to an authority, a chase cycle, a deadline cadence, and a refusal or review letter. THIS ROW is the records-holder's own disclosure process, in which the requester's identity is normally irrelevant to the answer and must never become a dimension. The casework row is an intermediary asking about one named person's own matter, where that person's identity is the whole basis of the request. RECIPROCAL and consistent with the landed casework node: if the chase seeks records under an access regime and the holder answers, it is this row; if it seeks a decision on a named individual's case on that individual's authority, it is casework.

SAME FIXTURE: FOI-2026-0412-export.zip and the released bundle inside it. The generic authority row holds the body's own function - the procurement evaluation, inspection report, or briefing that the bundle discloses. THIS ROW holds the request wrapper around those records. RECIPROCAL: the disclosed copies keep their own authority-side evidence and do not acquire request or release facts from membership here, and this row does not absorb a source record merely because a disclosure once quoted it. Where the wrapper is absent and only the underlying record survives, the generic authority row governs.

SAME FIXTURE: an item-by-item withholding table - Privilege Log - Acme v Beta - Set One.xlsx against FOI 2026-0412 - Schedule of Documents.xlsx. Both list document date, author, description, and a basis for withholding, and both accompany a redacted production. THIS ROW requires an external information request answered by a public body under an access process; the legal row requires a representation and a tribunal or discovery process. RECIPROCAL: a disclosure schedule is not a privilege log and a privilege log is not evidence of an access regime; neither row may claim the other's table from columnar shape.

falls_through_to.when: a readable standalone response letter, transfer notice, fee notice, review decision, or published disclosure-log extract has durable value but no accepted request lifecycle in the corpus
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: an unredacted source set, a schedule naming withheld material, a requester's inbound request, a case export, or an oversight submission lacks a safe accepted group; this is the default fallback for anything on the withheld side of the version family
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a redacted release, transparency report, or disclosure bundle appears to be reading material collected from an authority's publication scheme rather than held as its own case
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: an unheaded public-interest note, search record, or officer draft is partly understood but its request and holder role are unresolved
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a case export, redaction-tool project file, or bundle is password-protected, damaged, or in an unreadable format; the filename must not manufacture a request, requester, or release status
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced screen capture of a case queue or request portal yields no accepted request through OCR
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

sensitivity_why: This row is the one government situation whose packet is deliberately split in exposure, and getting that split wrong is the failure mode. The redacted release is prepared for publication; the unredacted source set, the schedule describing withheld material, the exemption rationale, and the requester's own identity are among the most protected things an authority holds - and the released copy and the withheld original are a version family, so any reasoning that propagates status across versions can leak the original. The requester is a named private individual whose interest is normally irrelevant to the answer, so their name must never become a display label, a group key, or a dimension. Released bundles also carry other people's personal data that survived redaction only because it was in scope. The design requires: “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.” Sensitivity here is only potentially_sensitive; P7 owns handling classes, and this node assigns none.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: three unresolved items, stated in the memo. (1) If PR-6 is lifted, decide centrally whether a bounded request reference may exist as a government field and whether it is destination-eligible; this row proposes no field so as not to pre-empt that adjudication. (2) Decide how P9 represents a version family whose members have opposite intended exposure, so that released status can never propagate from a redacted copy to its unredacted source. (3) Decide whether records disclosed inside a bundle are represented as members of the request with their own schema evidence intact, or as duplicates of corpus originals, or both; the choice determines whether a disclosure can retroactively change how an authority's own source record is displayed.
